citation: Temporal Technologies, State of Development 2026 report, temporal.io/reports/state-of-development-2026, survey run 29 April to 25 May 2026
source_tier: Vendor research (company-commissioned survey, run by Qualtrics)
access_status: Fully read via web fetch (page text summarised by a fetch tool, not a PDF); answer options for the trust question not shown on the page [uncertain]
sponsor_and_incentive: Commissioned by Temporal, which sells a durable-execution orchestrator marketed as making AI agents more reliable ('Develop AI agents 50% faster with an orchestrator that handles the tricky problems'). The report's top blockers (tracking state, debugging) map onto what Temporal sells. Temporal users are broken out and shown as more trusting (95.7% vs 84.7%).
exact_quotes: Question: 'How much do you trust the accuracy of AI agent outputs today?' (Chart 2.4, section 'What effect have AI agents had on you and your organization?'). 'One quarter (24.7%) completely trust the outputs.' Headline: '85.5% trust the outputs at least somewhat'. '41.1% encounter issues with AI agents daily or more' (Chart 2.6). 'Engineers need certainty that their delegates have done their job correctly.' 'The only way to know — beyond time-consuming testing and mathematical proofs — is to manually check.' (Chart 3.2 section). Free text: 'As long as humans remain responsible for validation.' Limitation: 'When we discuss those who are "successful at using AI agents," that is self-reported data.' Definition: 'AI agent = An LLM instance capable of taking multi-step actions on its own.'
date_and_recency: Data collected 29 April to 25 May 2026; report published 2026
key_claims: Most respondents trust agent output at least somewhat, yet a large share hit issues daily or more. Top blockers to using agents more are tracking state, debugging and managing costs. Trust is higher among self-described successful teams and Temporal users. Trust in the sense of putting your name on the commit is a separate bar from trusting enough to proceed.
headline_figures: 85.5% trust agent output at least somewhat (n=554, survey question on accuracy of outputs). 24.7% completely trust. 60.8% somewhat trust (the page words this as 'at least somewhat', but the arithmetic 85.5-24.7=60.8 shows it is somewhat-only) [uncertain]. 4.0% distrust. 41.1% encounter issues daily or more (Chart 2.6). Successful teams: 28.4% completely trust vs 4.7% others; 90.8% at least somewhat vs 57.0% [uncertain on exact category wording]. Temporal users 95.7% vs 84.7% somewhat or completely trust. Blockers: 79.8% say token and compute costs limit progress; 39.5% cite security as greatest blocker to truly autonomous agents (Chart 3.2). Top three blockers (Chart 3.1): tracking state, debugging, managing costs.
sample_unit_and_population: 554 retained respondents of 650 solicited (low-quality responses removed by authors). US and UK/EMEA, about two-thirds US. Software is the largest industry at 37.5%. Respondent role mix not confirmed [uncertain].
observed_vs_stated: Stated. Self-reported belief and self-reported issue frequency; 'successful' team status is also self-reported.
what_makes_trust_justified: Humans remain responsible for validation; manual checking of output; orchestration giving durable state and human-intervention triggers (the vendor's own pitch).
what_it_costs: Manual checking is described as the only certain route beyond 'time-consuming testing and mathematical proofs'. No time or cost figure for review is given on the page. Token and compute cost is a separate blocker (79.8%).
failure_mode_class: Over-reliance and wrong output (issues daily or more); security concerns (39.5%); state loss and debugging difficulty.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident report. The report points to human validation, state tracking and human-in-the-loop triggers.
limitations_stated: 'Successful' teams are self-reported. 'Each team may define issues differently.' Some findings flagged as needing more research (e.g. the isolation point). Low-quality responses removed (650 to 554).
counter_evidence: Vendor survey with commercial interest; no behavioural or observed data; trust measured by a single self-report question; 41.1% daily issues sits uneasily with 85.5% trust, which suggests trust is not tied to error rates. Only 4.0% distrust. Selection of respondents by Qualtrics panel unknown.
verification_status: Opened and read this session via fetch tool: trust question text, 85.5%, 24.7%, 41.1%, methodology dates, 554/650, blockers. Not confirmed: full answer option list, exact definition of 60.8% group, respondent role mix [uncertain]. No separate verification-rate statistic exists on the page.
usable_claim: In a Temporal-commissioned survey of 554 US and UK respondents (29 April to 25 May 2026), 85.5% said they trust agent output at least somewhat and 24.7% completely, while 41.1% said they hit issues with agents daily or more.
do_not_use: Do not treat the 60.8% as 'at least somewhat'. Do not present successful-team or Temporal-user trust gaps as causal. Do not claim the report measures verification practice. Do not present as independent research.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Unknown; not checked against the Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays [uncertain]
